comparisons.objective: Install and retain an inside-frame rack support bracket, versus loosen a captive nut and open an arm.
comparisons.physical_skill: Multi-feature bracket alignment/latching versus wrench selection, torque application, and arm rotation.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires unspecified mounting features engaged, correct OpenU, self-support, clearance, and no deformation; PR requires >60° nut backoff, arm ≥85°, damage avoidance, and a 20 s release hold.
comparisons.reason: Different objective, tool-mediated skill, and terminal state; the candidate’s missing latch thresholds do not suggest duplication.

comparisons.objective: Install a load-bearing bracket, versus push a trapped spacer out and recover it.
comparisons.physical_skill: Inside-frame alignment and retention versus indirect pushing through a constrained channel followed by pick-and-place.
comparisons.success_condition: Self-supporting registered bracket with no interference/deformation versus verified pusher-driven extraction, nested spacer, parked tool, and release dwell.
comparisons.reason: The tested causal manipulation and outcome are unrelated.

comparisons.objective: Install a rack support bracket, versus isolate a battery pack and remove busbars.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bracket registration/latching versus ordered electrical-service disassembly and avoidance of terminal hazards.
comparisons.success_condition: Engaged, self-supporting bracket versus plug removal followed by safe busbar/nut recovery without forbidden low passes or drops.
comparisons.reason: Different assembly direction, hazards, and success state.

comparisons.objective: Install a bracket, versus release a camera from a cam-clamped mount and place it on a pad.
comparisons.physical_skill: Multi-feature insertion/latching versus cam release, supported extraction, and careful placement.
comparisons.success_condition: Bracket retained at the correct rack level versus cam opened, payload cleared and stably placed without fixture movement or drop.
comparisons.reason: One creates a retained structural support; the other releases and removes a payload.

comparisons.objective: Install a rack bracket, versus release a screwdriver from a spring clamp and hold it.
comparisons.physical_skill: Inside-frame alignment/latching versus clamp release and controlled extraction while stabilizing the base.
comparisons.success_condition: Self-supporting bracket with all mounts engaged versus tool clear of the clamp, securely pinched at a target pose, with no base displacement or drop.
comparisons.reason: Different mechanism and endpoint despite both involving release-sensitive hardware.

comparisons.objective: Candidate installs a rack bracket; the record title indicates recovery from a clothing-obstructed drawer.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate proposes multi-feature latching; the record supplies no instruction or rubric from which its exact manipulation can be established.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate conditions are incomplete, and the record’s success conditions are entirely missing.
comparisons.reason: The apparent objectives differ, but missing record details prevent comparison across all required axes.

comparisons.objective: Install a rack bracket, versus buckle a doll into a car seat.
comparisons.physical_skill: Rigid structural registration/latching versus routing and engaging restraint tongues and a buckle clip around a body.
comparisons.success_condition: Bracket self-support and clearance versus both tongues and clip latched, correctly positioned, without seat movement or head intrusion.
comparisons.reason: Shared latching is generic; the restraint-routing ability and outcome are materially different.

comparisons.objective: Install a bracket, versus configure and operate a date stamp.
comparisons.physical_skill: Load-bearing part alignment/latching versus detented band rotation, inking, and controlled stamping.
comparisons.success_condition: Retained bracket at an OpenU versus correct date impression in a marked box and stamp returned.
comparisons.reason: No meaningful objective, skill, or scoring overlap.

comparisons.objective: Mount a rack support bracket, versus join and lock a click-floor tile to a laid row.
comparisons.physical_skill: Both may require elongated-part alignment and sequential engagement, but the tile specifically uses angled tongue insertion followed by lowering and seam closure; the candidate mechanism is unknown.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate calls for unspecified mounts engaged and self-support; PR measures seam, lippage, flatness, end gap, release, and damage.
comparisons.reason: The outcomes differ, but absent bracket CAD leaves open whether its core tested motion is the same angle-engage-and-lower locking sequence.

comparisons.objective: Install an IT support bracket in a rack, versus level a rack shelf by relocating one pull pin.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate proposes whole-bracket multi-feature alignment/latching; PR extracts, aligns, and reseats one load-support pin while preserving three others.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires correct OpenU and all unknown mounts engaged; PR requires four pins seated at level 2 and the shelf level, with movement limits on the other pins.
comparisons.reason: Both concern rack support registration and retention, and the candidate’s undisclosed interface prevents ruling out the same pin/hole ability.

comparisons.objective: Install a bracket, versus hand-fit an oil filter.
comparisons.physical_skill: Multi-feature rack alignment/latching versus thread starting and controlled gasket compression by rotation.
comparisons.success_condition: Self-supporting bracket versus prescribed rotation after gasket contact without cross-threading, removal, looseness, or overtightening.
comparisons.reason: Threaded sealing and torque-by-angle are absent from the candidate.

comparisons.objective: Install a rigid rack bracket, versus mount the final section of a bicycle tire bead.
comparisons.physical_skill: Rigid feature registration versus coordinated deformation, bead-channel management, and bimanual rolling without a lever.
comparisons.success_condition: Bracket engagement/self-support versus bead fully seated without prohibited lever use or damage.
comparisons.reason: The PR tests deformable manipulation that the rigid bracket task does not.

comparisons.objective: Install and retain a rack bracket, versus lower a bent tube into a checking fixture.
comparisons.physical_skill: Both involve bimanual handling of an elongated rigid part and simultaneous multi-feature alignment; the PR stops at gravity seating, while the candidate additionally claims tool-less locking.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate needs unspecified mounts engaged and structural self-support; PR requires all four legs seated in slots, released, and still.
comparisons.reason: There is substantial alignment overlap, and without bracket geometry it is impossible to show that locking adds a meaningfully different tested ability.

comparisons.objective: Install a bracket, versus shim a door jamb.
comparisons.physical_skill: Rigid bracket registration/latching versus opposed insertion of tapered wedges with force balance to close a gap without bowing.
comparisons.success_condition: Bracket retained and clear versus paired shims snug after release within jamb-bow and alignment limits.
comparisons.reason: Opposed wedging and compliance/force balancing are materially different.

comparisons.objective: Install a rack bracket, versus sort cubes while yielding to a human hand.
comparisons.physical_skill: Constrained structural assembly versus pick-and-place with dynamic human-aware exclusion and waiting.
comparisons.success_condition: Bracket engagement/self-support versus correctly sorted cubes with no bin entry, proximity breach, or human contact during hand intrusion.
comparisons.reason: The PR’s central tested ability is safety-aware coordination, not mechanical retention.

comparisons.objective: Install a bracket, versus fit and bolt an inside-bolt-circle gasket between flanges.
comparisons.physical_skill: Tool-less bracket alignment/latching versus flexible gasket placement and sequential bolt insertion around a flange.
comparisons.success_condition: Correct OpenU, all mounts engaged, and no interference versus centred flat gasket, four inserted bolts, release, and stillness.
comparisons.reason: The flange task tests gasket positioning and bolt insertion; generic multi-hole alignment alone does not prove overlap.

comparisons.objective: Install a retained rack bracket, versus seat a platform on three kinematic datums.
comparisons.physical_skill: Both require multi-feature rigid-part alignment and level lowering; candidate additionally asserts sequential hooks/latches, but those features are undocumented.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires unknown mounts locked and self-supporting; PR requires three matched supports bearing load within tight pose/force tolerances after release.
comparisons.reason: The shared core may be multi-datum seating, and absent candidate CAD prevents establishing a distinct retention challenge.

comparisons.objective: Install a rack bracket, versus refit a loaded drawer onto cabinet slides and verify it by closing and pull-testing.
comparisons.physical_skill: Both may require bimanual support of an elongated/load-bearing component, constrained guided alignment, hook clearance, engagement, and release.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires unknown mounts engaged at an OpenU; PR requires drawer riding on both slides, closed hands-off, then reopened about 5 cm without losing its load.
comparisons.reason: Potentially close guided support-hardware installation; the candidate lacks the geometry needed to prove a different insertion or latch ability.

comparisons.objective: Install a bracket, versus open an ampoule with a protective captive opener.
comparisons.physical_skill: Structural alignment/latching versus controlled brittle-joint breaking while retaining the cap and stabilizing the body.
comparisons.success_condition: Self-supporting bracket versus confirmed neck break, upright returned body, cap retained in the opener, and hands released.
comparisons.reason: Fracture control and fragment containment are unique to the PR.

comparisons.objective: Install and retain a rack bracket, versus assemble and retain a chain joint with a forked keeper plate.
comparisons.physical_skill: Both involve aligning multiple rigid features and sequentially engaging a retention element; the candidate’s hook/slot/latch mechanics are unspecified.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires every unknown mount engaged and bracket self-support; PR requires both chain holes on pins, keeper stems in retained slot regions, cradle placement, clearance, and dwell.
comparisons.reason: A plausible duplicate exists at the level of multi-pin/slot alignment followed by lateral retention, and candidate evidence cannot resolve it.

comparisons.objective: Install a rack bracket, versus place setting blocks and glaze a window frame.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual elongated-part alignment is shared generically, but the PR requires staged block placement and vertical lowering of fragile glass without sill contact.
comparisons.success_condition: Bracket locked and clear versus glass standing on both correctly placed blocks, centred and released, with any sill touch invalidating the run.
comparisons.reason: The staged support preparation and fragile-contact constraint test a materially different ability.

comparisons.objective: Tool-less bracket installation, versus insert and tighten a bracket bolt with a confined-access ratchet.
comparisons.physical_skill: Unknown hook/latch engagement versus thread capture, socket engagement, short-stroke ratcheting, and torque/seat control.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate needs all tool-less mounts engaged; PR requires bolt advancement, bracket seating, ratchet cycles or target torque, tool removal, and release. Some PR versions state live scoring is unqualified.
comparisons.reason: Both secure brackets, but the tested physical abilities are materially different; the PR’s incomplete scorer qualification is noted.

comparisons.objective: Install a bracket, versus polish both faces of a blank on a powered buffing wheel.
comparisons.physical_skill: Rigid alignment/latching versus force-controlled surface coverage, regrasping/flipping, and avoidance of wheel snatch.
comparisons.success_condition: Retained bracket versus sufficient polishing of both faces, no snatch/fling event, and stable return to the rack.
comparisons.reason: No meaningful physical-skill or endpoint overlap.

comparisons.objective: Install a rack bracket, versus reattach a camera to a wrist mount.
comparisons.physical_skill: Both may require constrained guided insertion, precision alignment, latch engagement, and hands-free retention; candidate mount details are absent.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires unknown mounts engaged, correct level, self-support, and clearance; PR requires camera pose alignment, verified channel entry/seating/latching, live image delivery, and a 2 s released hold.
comparisons.reason: The camera task plausibly exercises the same align-insert-latch-release primitive, and missing bracket CAD prevents proving meaningful distinction.

comparisons.objective: Install a rigid bracket, versus fit an O-ring into a hydraulic plug groove.
comparisons.physical_skill: Rigid multi-feature alignment/latching versus controlled elastic stretching, sliding over threads, untwisted seating, and careful release.
comparisons.success_condition: Bracket self-support/no deformation versus ring fully seated square and untwisted without exceeding the irreversible 50% stretch limit.
comparisons.reason: The PR tests validated deformable manipulation and damage limits absent from the candidate.
